solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Types who might host lifeless parties? (8)

annotation.definition: Types who might host lifeless parties?

blocks.note: people who might hold a gathering; nothing here yet says what kind
the surface pushes dull, boring parties; the setter means parties attended by the literally lifeless, the dead

annotation.surface: A dig at the sort of people whose gatherings are dull and dead.
annotation.walkthrough: "Lifeless parties" reads as dull get-togethers, but here it means parties of the dead: a psychic medium hosts a séance where the guests have passed on.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a séance is a gathering of the living and the dead, and psychic mediums are the ones who hold them.

entries.clue: Can good boy put across whopper ultimately? (6)

indicatorNotes.put across: PI is laid across R, holding it in the middle
indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the final letter of whopper

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether a well-behaved lad could get away with a big lie.
annotation.walkthrough: "Can" looks like the verb opening a question; it is the noun, slang for jail.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense, mainly American: to be in the can is to be locked up in jail.

entries.clue: Unknown, head-shaven hip-hop artist Lil’ Dog? (6)

indicatorNotes.head-shaven: a head shaved off loses its first letter

blocks.note: algebra's unknowns are x, y and z

annotation.surface: A little-known rapper with a shaved head and a stage name in the style of Lil Wayne.
annotation.walkthrough: The rap-name styling of "Lil’ Dog" hides a plain small dog; the question mark flags that a yapper is just one sort.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: little dogs are notorious for shrill barking, or yapping, so a small dog is a typical yapper.

entries.clue: Possibly suffering with temperature or rash (3-6)

blocks.note: taken literally, someone with a fever has a hot head; 'possibly' flags the playful reading
rash here is the adjective, reckless and impetuous

annotation.surface: A patient with a fever or a skin rash, as a doctor might list symptoms.
annotation.walkthrough: Read literally, a hot head is what a fever gives you; "rash" looks like a spot on the skin but means reckless.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: the everyday idiom for a quick-tempered, reckless person, and a whimsical literal reading of a feverish head.

entries.clue: Obedient monkey with belt on collar (12)

indicatorNotes.monkey with: to monkey with something is to tamper with it, messing up its letters

annotation.surface: Advice on training a pet: a monkey on a lead with a belt fixed to its collar will behave.
annotation.walkthrough: "Monkey" looks like the animal wearing the collar; with "with" it is a verb meaning tamper.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: an obedient animal or person does what it is told, so it is easy to keep in check.

entries.clue: Criminal cur undergoing change of heart (6)

indicatorNotes.undergoing change of heart: the middle letters are swapped for others

blocks.note: a rotter is a cad, a cur

annotation.surface: A villain who has a sudden change of heart and reforms.
annotation.walkthrough: A "change of heart" is usually repentance; here it is literal, the two middle letters of ROTTER replaced.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a robber, who steals by force or threat, is one particular kind of criminal.

entries.clue: Outstanding oarsmanship won’t be topped (5)

indicatorNotes.won’t be topped: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which is removed

annotation.surface: Praise for superb rowing that no one will ever better.
annotation.walkthrough: "Outstanding" reads as praise for the rowing; it means unpaid, and "won’t be topped" is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: The accounting sense: an unpaid bill is both outstanding and owing, not the 'excellent' sense the surface uses.

entries.clue: Country song that line-snorting fan’s put on (8)

indicatorNotes.snorting: the fan takes the line in, as a snort goes up the nose
indicatorNotes.put on: in a down entry, BULG is placed on top of ARIA

blocks.note: a bug is an enthusiast, as in the travel bug
an aria is an operatic song

annotation.surface: A country-music number that a cocaine-using fan puts on the stereo.
annotation.walkthrough: "Country song" reads as one phrase for a genre; the first word is the definition, and "line-snorting" is drug slang turned into a container.
annotation.definitionFit: Bulgaria is a country in south-east Europe.

entries.clue: Taxpayer? Trump has been one, Pence let slip (8)

indicatorNotes.let slip: the P is allowed to slip away

blocks.note: Donald Trump has been US president

annotation.surface: A political jibe: Trump was president, and Mike Pence let something slip about his taxes.
annotation.walkthrough: Mike Pence, Trump's vice-president, is a decoy; "Pence" is just the money abbreviation P. The question mark marks "taxpayer" as one example of a resident.
annotation.definitionFit: A resident of a country is typically liable to pay its taxes.

entries.clue: Weak spirit served with old Spanish wine (8)

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous spirit
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

annotation.surface: A bar order: a watered-down spirit served alongside an aged Spanish wine.
annotation.walkthrough: "Weak spirit" looks like a thin drink; the spirit is an imp. Tent is an old name for a red wine from Spain.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in its general sense: lacking power or strength, as in an impotent protest.

entries.clue: Piece of agricultural land with small WC? (6)

annotation.definitionNote: W.C. Fields, the American comic actor

blocks.note: a field is a piece of farmland

annotation.surface: A plot of farmland that comes with a little outdoor toilet.
annotation.walkthrough: WC looks like water closet; it is the initials of W.C. Fields, the American comedian and film star of the 1930s.
annotation.definitionFit: W.C. Fields is the man identified by the initials WC.

entries.clue: One getting shot of awfully spare romance (12)

indicatorNotes.awfully: the letters are arranged badly and need rearranging

annotation.surface: A spurned lover getting rid of a dreadful spare love affair.
annotation.walkthrough: "Getting shot of" is British slang for getting rid of; split after "shot", the shot is a camera take.
annotation.definitionFit: A cameraperson is the one who gets the shots on film.

entries.clue: Very big award presented by Asher on occasion (5)

indicatorNotes.on occasion: only some of Asher's letters appear, every other one

blocks.note: OBE: Officer of the Order of the British Empire, an honour
the second and fourth letters of ASHER

annotation.surface: A major honour handed out by someone named Asher from time to time.
annotation.walkthrough: "Very big award" reads as one phrase; the definition stops at "big". The OBE is a British honour given by the monarch.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, applied to body size: grossly overweight is a polite way of saying very big.

entries.clue: Military detachment in a bulletproof SEAT? (9)

annotation.definition: Military detachment in a bulletproof SEAT?

blocks.note: a unit of troops, read straight
the surface pushes an armoured SEAT car; the setter means a guard that makes your seat, your rear, bulletproof

annotation.surface: A squad of soldiers riding in an armoured car, SEAT being a Spanish car make.
annotation.walkthrough: SEAT in capitals suggests the car brand; it is the backside, and a guard over your seat, protecting it from bullets, is a rear guard.
annotation.definitionFit: A rearguard is the detachment protecting the back of an army.

entries.clue: Man helping to limit energy pollution (12)

indicatorNotes.to limit: ADULT and RATION together close in the E between them

blocks.note: a man is a grown-up, an adult
a ration is a portion, a helping

annotation.surface: A man doing his bit to cut energy use and reduce pollution.
annotation.walkthrough: "Helping to limit" reads as assisting; "helping" is a noun, a serving of food.
annotation.definitionFit: Adulteration is the contamination, pollution, of something pure.

entries.clue: I’d balance out one giving pushback in Barnet (5,4)

indicatorNotes.out: the letters are out of their order

annotation.surface: A peacemaker in the London borough of Barnet promising to even out opposition.
annotation.walkthrough: Barnet looks like the London borough; it is rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair). An Alice band is a headband that holds the hair back.
annotation.definitionFit: An Alice band pushes the hair back from the face.

entries.clue: Most sharp way in which regular hit revolutionary (8)

indicatorNotes.in which: the way is the thing the rest goes in
indicatorNotes.revolutionary: a revolution is a full turn, so a revolutionary phrase is turned round to read backwards

annotation.surface: A news line about the cleverest method by which a regular fighter struck a rebel.
annotation.walkthrough: "Revolutionary" looks like the person hit, a rebel; it is only an instruction. "Regular hit" hides two words, and the reversal applies to both together.
annotation.definitionFit: Smartest means sharpest, most quick-witted.

entries.clue: Make light of drama over drink (4,4)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down entry, PLAY sits above DOWN

blocks.note: to down a drink is to swallow it

annotation.surface: Laughing off a scene someone made about a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: "Drama over drink" suggests a row in a pub; "drink" is the verb, as in down a pint.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom match: both phrasal verbs mean treating something as less important than it is.

entries.clue: I am told cream crackers can be sensational (12)

indicatorNotes.crackers: crazy, so the letters go wild

annotation.surface: Hearsay that cream crackers, the plain biscuits, can taste wonderful.
annotation.walkthrough: Cream crackers are plain savoury biscuits, so the phrase reads as one thing; split it and "crackers" means mad.
annotation.definitionFit: Melodramatic means sensational, exaggerated for effect.

entries.clue: Commercial bishop and vicar turned over quickly? (6)

annotation.definitionNote: an example of the answer: the word "quickly" is an adverb

indicatorNotes.turned over: flipped, so the letters read backwards

annotation.surface: An advert showing a bishop and a vicar being knocked over at speed.
annotation.walkthrough: "Quickly" seems to describe how they were turned over; it is the definition, a word of the kind the answer names.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: quickly is a typical -ly adverb, and the question mark admits it is one of many.

entries.clue: Angry European will get stick (6)

annotation.surface: A furious European is going to get a beating with a stick.
annotation.walkthrough: "Get stick" is British slang for being criticised; here the stick is a real one, used in lacrosse.
annotation.definitionFit: A crosse is the netted stick used in lacrosse.

entries.clue: A shade right-wing, like Edward III primarily (5,4)

blocks.note: Edward III was, first and foremost, royal: a king
blue is the colour of the British Conservatives

annotation.surface: A historian calling a medieval king slightly conservative.
annotation.walkthrough: "A shade right-wing" reads as slightly conservative; "a shade" is the definition, a colour. In Britain the right-wing Conservatives are the blues.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: this deep, vivid blue is one of many named colours, and shade is used loosely for colour.

entries.clue: With vacuous leader round, time for a drink (5)

indicatorNotes.vacuous: emptied, leaving only the outer letters
indicatorNotes.round: round as a preposition means encircling, so these letters wrap around the next piece

blocks.note: an age is a long time

annotation.surface: With an empty-headed boss buying a round, it is time for a pint.
annotation.walkthrough: "Round" looks like a round of drinks, which fits the pub surface perfectly; it is a placement instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: lager, a pale fizzy beer, is one example of a drink.

entries.clue: Energy one gets with flipping wine one downed (5)

indicatorNotes.flipping: turned over, so RED reads backwards

blocks.note: E = energy, then I = one, the Roman numeral

annotation.surface: Someone gets a burst of energy from a glass of wine they have knocked back.
annotation.walkthrough: "Downed" reads as drunk; it means covered in down, and the eider duck's down fills eiderdowns.
annotation.definitionFit: The eider is a sea duck prized for its soft down.

entries.clue: Adequate nurse has cold symptom, but no cold (6)

indicatorNotes.but no: the symptom is taken without its C

blocks.note: a cough comes with a cold
C = cold, as on taps; removed

annotation.surface: A decent nurse with a cough but, oddly, no cold.
annotation.walkthrough: "Adequate nurse" reads as a so-so nurse; the definition is the first word alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean sufficient for the need, as in adequate or enough food.

entries.clue: Breakout artists Keys introduces close to stage (8)

indicatorNotes.introduces: the keys bring the E inside themselves
indicatorNotes.close to: take the final letter of stage

annotation.surface: A pop news item: singer Alicia Keys brings a new act on at the end of the show.
annotation.walkthrough: Keys looks like Alicia Keys introducing breakout acts; the keys are escape keys, and "breakout artists" are jailbreakers.
annotation.definitionFit: Escapees are people who break out of prison.

entries.clue: Plain fish without starters in Dutch restaurant (6)

indicatorNotes.without: outside: TUNA sits around the letters
indicatorNotes.starters: the first letters of the next two words

blocks.note: first letters of Dutch and restaurant

annotation.surface: A complaint about bland fish served with no appetisers at a Dutch restaurant.
annotation.walkthrough: "Plain fish" reads as simple food and "without starters" as skipping the first course; "without" means outside.
annotation.definitionFit: Tundra is a vast treeless Arctic plain.

entries.clue: One bleedin’ criminal not fit to be put away (8)

annotation.definition: not fit to be put away

indicatorNotes.criminal: the letters are treated criminally, rearranged

annotation.surface: A cockney grumbling about a villain who ought to be locked up.
annotation.walkthrough: "Put away" reads as sent to prison; it means eaten, as in putting away a big meal.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to put away food is to eat a lot of it, so something not fit to be put away cannot be eaten.
